title: Why companies acquire
objectives: Answer out loud: Why would a company acquire another?
Answer out loud: Why are revenue synergies discounted?

steps.body: Buy growth faster than building it.
Synergies: cost (cutting overlapping functions, purchasing power) and revenue (cross-selling, new markets).
Gain market share or remove a competitor.

blocks.template: {{1}} synergies are more reliable than {{2}} synergies

blocks.title: Why would a company acquire instead of build?
blocks.teaser: Speed, certainty (the target already works), access to customers or IP that would take years to build, and sometimes it's cheaper than organic invest…
blocks.body:
Speed, certainty (the target already works), access to customers or IP that would take years to build, and sometimes it's cheaper than organic investment.

**Interview answer:** "Speed and certainty — the target already has the product, customers, or capabilities, which could take years to build internally."

blocks.title: Why are cost synergies valued more than revenue synergies?
blocks.teaser: Cost synergies are within management's control (closing a duplicate office, merging systems).
blocks.body: Cost synergies are within management's control (closing a duplicate office, merging systems). Revenue synergies depend on customers' behavior and frequently fail to materialize. Bankers and investors often discount or exclude revenue synergies.

blocks.prompt: Why do bankers trust cost synergies more than revenue synergies?

options.text: Cost synergies are within management's control; revenue synergies depend on customers
Cost synergies happen immediately with no integration costs

blocks.explanation: Closing a duplicate office is in management's control; getting customers to buy more is not — revenue synergies often fail to materialize.

blocks.title: Why do many acquisitions destroy value?
blocks.teaser: Overpaying (the winner's curse in competitive auctions), overestimated synergies, integration problems, and culture clashes.
blocks.body: Overpaying (the winner's curse in competitive auctions), overestimated synergies, integration problems, and culture clashes.

blocks.title: What's the difference between a strategic and a financial buyer?
blocks.teaser: A strategic buyer is an operating company buying to grow or combine its business.
blocks.body: A strategic buyer is an operating company buying to grow or combine its business. A financial buyer (PE firm) buys to generate a return over a holding period, typically using leverage, and plans to exit.
